description: Visual diff of two pages or two existing screenshots. Use it to verify a change did what you intended and nothing else moved: before/after a deploy, staging vs production, or one page at two points in time. Each side is either `{url}` (captured now) or `{screenshot_url}` (an earlier GetScreenshot result, reused at no cost; it is checked before any capture is spent). To compare a page across a change, capture it first, make the change, then pass the earlier screenshot_url as `before` and the page url as `after`. Returns the percentage of changed pixels, the bounding box of the changed area, and a diff image: the after image dimmed, changed pixels in magenta, a red rectangle around the changed area. When nothing changed no image is attached. Costs 1 screenshot of the monthly quota per side given as `url` (0 to 2 per call). Both sides are captured with the same viewport options. Takes about 9-25 seconds when it captures. Limits: pages must be publicly reachable. At most the top 2,400 px are compared (at up to 1280 px wide); for a lower part of a long page, capture that part of both versions with capture_screenshot and `element`, then compare the two screenshot_url values. Animations, ads and rotating content show up as differences; hide them with hide_selectors.

after.description: The "after" image. Provide exactly one of url or screenshot_url.

screenshot_url.description: The screenshot_url of an earlier GetScreenshot capture (uses no quota). Only GetScreenshot storage URLs are accepted.

url.description: A public page URL to capture now (uses 1 screenshot of quota).

before.description: The "before" image. Provide exactly one of url or screenshot_url.

screenshot_url.description: The screenshot_url of an earlier GetScreenshot capture (uses no quota). Only GetScreenshot storage URLs are accepted.

url.description: A public page URL to capture now (uses 1 screenshot of quota).

device.description: Device preset: sets the viewport and, for phones, a mobile user agent. Overrides width and height. iphone* and pixel* are phones, ipad* are tablets, the rest are fixed desktop sizes.

full_page.description: Capture whole pages instead of the viewport. Applies to sides given as url.

height.description: Viewport height in CSS pixels. API default 800. Ignored when device is set.

hide_selectors.description: CSS selector(s) to hide in both captures. Use it to remove things that change on every load (ads, carousels, timestamps) so they do not show up as differences.

threshold.description: Per-pixel colour tolerance from 0 (any difference counts) to 1 (nothing counts). Default 0.1 ignores anti-aliasing noise.

wait_ms.description: Extra wait in milliseconds after load, before the capture. API default 2000. Raise it for late animations or client-side rendering.

wait_until.description: When the page counts as loaded. API default "networkidle2". Use "domcontentloaded" for heavy or slow sites (fastest, most reliable); "networkidle0" waits for all network activity to stop.

width.description: Viewport width in CSS pixels. API default 1280. Ignored when device is set.

name: compare_screenshots

origin_url.description: Page that was captured; null when an existing screenshot was supplied.
Page that was captured; null when an existing screenshot was supplied.

bounding_box.description: Smallest rectangle containing all changed pixels, in comparison-image pixels. Null when nothing changed.

changed_percent.description: Share of compared pixels that differ, 0-100.

compared.description: Size both images were normalised to before comparing.

estimated_image_tokens.description: Approximate total vision tokens of the inline images.

expires_in_days.description: Stored files are deleted after this many days.

identical.description: True when no compared pixel differs and both images have exactly the same width and height.

images.description: One entry per inline image, in the same order as the image blocks.

index.description: 0-based position of the slice, top to bottom.

y.description: Top offset of this image within the downscaled capture, in the same pixels as width/height.

size_changed.description: True when the two images differ in size, for example the page got taller.

total_slices.description: How many slices the whole image needs at this detail level, whether or not they are attached. With return: "url_only" this is how many a normal call would produce.

truncated.description: True when images were requested and some slices were left out, because of max_slices or the inline size limit. Always false with return: "url_only", where no image is attached by request.

warnings.description: Things worth knowing about this result, for example an error status from the page.
